settings.description: Cost assumptions, the tenant entitlement, OneDrive storage per user and when a site counts as inactive. Saved in this browser only.
settings.rateHint: Used for the cost of doing nothing, the growth cost and the potential saving.
settings.entitlementHint: Estimated from licences: {estimate}. Enter the figure from the SharePoint admin centre to replace it; clear it to go back to the estimate.
settings.entitlementHintNoEstimate: Enter the figure from the SharePoint admin centre.
settings.oneDriveEntitlementHint: From licences: {estimate} {unit} — the most generous plan in the tenant (5 TB on E3, E5, G3 and G5 with five or more licences, 1 TB on Business plans, 2 GB on frontline). Enter a figure to replace it; clear it to go back to the estimate.
settings.oneDriveEntitlementHintNoEstima: What each user licence includes: 5 TB on E3, E5, G3 and G5 with five or more licences, 1 TB on Business plans, 2 GB on frontline.
settings.oneDriveEntitlementHintDriveLim: What each user licence includes: 5 TB on E3, E5, G3 and G5 with five or more licences, 1 TB on Business plans, 2 GB on frontline. Left empty, drives are measured against the commonest OneDrive limit.
settings.oneDriveEntitlementHintNoLimit: What each user licence includes: 5 TB on E3, E5, G3 and G5 with five or more licences, 1 TB on Business plans, 2 GB on frontline. Left empty, no OneDrive is measured against a limit: neither the licences nor the OneDrives give one.
settings.oneDriveEntitlementHintUnread: What each user licence includes: 5 TB on E3, E5, G3 and G5 with five or more licences, 1 TB on Business plans, 2 GB on frontline. The OneDrive usage report did not come back this time, so no OneDrive is measured until it does.
settings.inactiveYearsHint: A site with no activity for this long counts as ready to archive, and a OneDrive as inactive. Default {years} years.

auth.notAssigned.title: Your account is not allowed to use this app
auth.notAssigned.body: Your organisation limits this report to chosen users or groups, and your account is not one of them. An administrator can add you under the app's Users and groups in Microsoft Entra.

auth.consent.body: This report only reads Microsoft 365 data, but a Global Administrator has to grant admin consent once before anyone in your tenant can use it.
auth.consent.linkTail: — you will be asked to review the read-only permissions this report needs, then returned here.
errors.insufficientPermissions: Insufficient permissions — admin consent or the required role may be needed for this report.
access.consent.title: Your organisation has not approved this app yet
access.consent.body: Approving sign-in is not enough: the report reads your tenant with application permissions, which a Global Administrator has to grant once for the whole tenant. Signing in again will not help until they do.
access.consent.delegatedBody: The report reads usage reports as you, and your organisation has not granted it that permission yet — signing in does not grant it, and no role of yours changes that. A Global Administrator has to grant admin consent once for the whole tenant.
access.permissions.intro: The grant covers these read-only permissions, and Microsoft lists the same ones on its consent page:
access.permissions.reports: Microsoft 365 usage reports: storage per site and per OneDrive, and who holds a OneDrive licence
access.permissions.organization: tenant name and licences, for the storage entitlement and OneDrive storage per user
access.tenant.title: This tenant is not enabled for the report yet
access.tenant.body: You signed in successfully, but your tenant has not been switched on for this report. No role or consent will change that — ask Proventeq to enable it.
access.permission.title: Your account cannot read usage reports
access.permission.body: You are signed in and your organisation has approved the app, but reading tenant usage reports needs an administrative role. Microsoft requires Global Reader, Reports Reader, or an equivalent role — ask an administrator to assign one.

helpButton.label: About {title}
table.column.help.site: The site's display name and a link to it, looked up in the tenant site directory because Microsoft's usage report leaves the URL blank. A site the signed-in account cannot open, or one that has been deleted, shows its owner and site id instead.
table.column.help.drive: The OneDrive account, named after its owner, with a link to the drive.
table.column.help.owner: The primary owner as Microsoft's usage report records it. For group-connected sites this is the Microsoft 365 group's owners.
table.column.help.files: Files stored, as of the report date.
table.column.help.active: Files that were created, edited or otherwise active during the 180-day reporting period.
table.column.help.used: Storage consumed, as Microsoft's usage report measures it, as of the report date.
table.column.help.share: This row's storage as a percentage of its own pool: a site's share of all SharePoint storage in use, a OneDrive's share of all OneDrive storage in use. The bar is drawn to the same scale. A pool that holds no storage at all gives each of its rows 0.0%; shares that would round to 0.0% or 100.0% read <0.1% and >99.9%.
table.column.help.lastActivity: The most recent day with file activity in the 180-day reporting period. Never means no activity was recorded in that period.
table.column.help.template: The SharePoint template the site was created from, or Template not reported when Microsoft's usage report gives none. Team Channel and Group templates count as Teams in the workload split; everything else counts as SharePoint.
table.column.help.capacity: How much of the drive's own storage quota is used — the limit a OneDrive actually stops at. Blank for sites, whose allocation is the 25 TB site-collection maximum rather than a quota, and for a OneDrive that reports no limit.
table.column.help.overEntitlement: How much more the drive holds than the OneDrive storage per user this report measures against.
table.column.help.overDriveLimit: How much more the drive holds than the commonest OneDrive limit, which this report measures against when no licence or setting gives the storage per user.

storageOptimisation.description: A consolidated summary of tenant storage — where it sits today, where it is heading, and what drives it.
storageOptimisation.capacity.title: Tenant capacity
storageOptimisation.kpi.archivableHint: {percent} of SharePoint storage, in {sites} {count, plural, one {site} other {sites}} with no activity for {years, plural, one {# year} other {# years}} (since {date}).
storageOptimisation.kpi.archivableNoneHi: No site has gone {years, plural, one {# year} other {# years}} without activity (since {date}).
storageOptimisation.kpi.savingHint: Storage cost avoided if the {size} of inactive sites is archived, valued at {rate}/GB per month.
storageOptimisation.kpi.savingOverHint: Spend avoided by archiving inactive sites: {saved} of the {overage} over your entitlement, valued at {rate}/GB per month.
storageOptimisation.kpi.savingNoneHint: Nothing to save until a site passes the inactivity threshold in Report settings.
storageOptimisation.kpi.costOfNothing: Cost of doing nothing, next 12 months
storageOptimisation.kpi.costOfNothingHin: Extra spend over the next 12 months on growth beyond your entitlement, valued at {rate}/GB per month. Zero while growth stays within it.
storageOptimisation.kpi.forecastHint: The month SharePoint storage passes your {entitled} entitlement if it keeps growing {growth} a month. {remaining} of headroom is left.
storageOptimisation.kpi.forecastBeyondHo: At {growth} a month, the {remaining} of headroom left under your {entitled} entitlement lasts more than {years} years.
storageOptimisation.kpi.forecastNoGrowth: SharePoint storage has not grown over the last {months} months, so it is not on course to pass your {entitled} entitlement.
SharePoint storage has not grown over the last {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}, so it is not on course to pass your {entitled} entitlement.
storageOptimisation.kpi.growthPerMonthHi: {used} of SharePoint storage, changing by {growth} a month over {window}. Enter the tenant entitlement in Options, Report settings to forecast it against the entitlement.
storageOptimisation.distribution.title: Current storage distribution
storageOptimisation.distribution.subtitl: Where storage sits today — every SharePoint workload against your SharePoint entitlement, OneDrive as its own pool, and which site types drive the volume
Where storage sits today, from the Microsoft reports that came back
storageOptimisation.usage.title: Storage usage
storageOptimisation.usage.subtitle: Every SharePoint workload on one line, ending in what is left of your SharePoint entitlement. OneDrive is a separate pool, shown below. Hover or select a part for details.
storageOptimisation.usage.subtitleNoEnti: Every SharePoint workload on one line. OneDrive is a separate pool, shown below. Hover or select a part for details.
storageOptimisation.usage.subtitleAlone: Every SharePoint workload on one line, ending in what is left of your SharePoint entitlement. OneDrive is a separate pool. Hover or select a part for details.
storageOptimisation.usage.subtitleNoEnti: Every SharePoint workload on one line. OneDrive is a separate pool. Hover or select a part for details.
storageOptimisation.usage.sharePointAllD: All SharePoint storage in use, from the SharePoint storage trend, Teams, inactive and deleted sites included: the site usage report that splits them out did not come back this time. Counts against your SharePoint entitlement.
storageOptimisation.usage.headline: of the {entitled} SharePoint entitlement used ({used})
storageOptimisation.usage.enterEntitleme: Enter the tenant entitlement in Options, Report settings to see how much of it is left.
storageOptimisation.usage.describe.share: Live SharePoint sites with recent activity. Counts against your SharePoint entitlement.
storageOptimisation.usage.describe.teams: Live sites created from Teams channel and group templates, with recent activity. Counts against your SharePoint entitlement.
storageOptimisation.usage.describe.delet: {count, plural, =0 {No deleted site is held.} one {# deleted site is still held, and counts against the entitlement, until Microsoft's retention period ends.} other {# deleted sites are still held, and count against the entitlement, until Microsoft's retention period ends.}}
storageOptimisation.usage.describe.inact: Live sites with no activity for {years, plural, one {# year} other {# years}} (since {date}). Archiving them frees this space.
storageOptimisation.usage.describe.versi: Microsoft's usage reports count version history inside each site's storage, without splitting it out. Proventeq 365 measures it library by library.
storageOptimisation.usage.describe.free: What is left of the {entitled} SharePoint entitlement.
storageOptimisation.usage.describe.freeO: Nothing is left: SharePoint storage is {overage} over the {entitled} entitlement.
storageOptimisation.oneDrivePool.title: Live OneDrive storage
storageOptimisation.oneDrivePool.subtitl: A separate pool: each user's OneDrive has its own allowance from their licence, so it does not use the SharePoint entitlement above.
A separate pool: each user's OneDrive has its own allowance from their licence, so it does not use the SharePoint entitlement.
storageOptimisation.oneDrivePool.headlin: of the {allocated} allocated to {count, plural, one {# OneDrive} other {# OneDrives}} used ({used})
of the {allocated} allocated to the {count, plural, one {# OneDrive that reports} other {# OneDrives that report}} a limit used ({used})
storageOptimisation.oneDrivePool.without: {count, plural, one {# live OneDrive} other {# live OneDrives}} holding {bytes} {count, plural, one {reports} other {report}} no limit and {count, plural, one {is} other {are}} left out of this line.
storageOptimisation.oneDrivePool.noLimit: {used} in {count, plural, one {# live OneDrive} other {# live OneDrives}}. Microsoft's usage report gives no storage limit for them, so there is no allocation to draw them against.
storageOptimisation.oneDrivePool.attenti: Kept apart, never added together: inactive OneDrives hold {inactive}, deleted ones under retention {deleted}, and those of owners without a OneDrive licence {unlicensed}{notListed, plural, =0 {} one { (# owner inferred from not being in Microsoft's licence report)} other { (# owners inferred from not being in Microsoft's licence report)}}. Unlicensed and retained deleted OneDrives can be billed once Microsoft archives them.

Kept apart, never added together: inactive OneDrives hold {inactive}, deleted ones under retention {deleted}, and {quiet} sits in OneDrives with no activity for over {days} days. Microsoft's active-user report did not come back or matched none of the owners, so the quiet ones stand in for the owners without a licence. Unlicensed and retained deleted OneDrives can be billed once Microsoft archives them.
storageOptimisation.oneDrivePool.none: No live OneDrive is in Microsoft's usage report.
storageOptimisation.oneDrivePool.trendOn: {used} stored in OneDrive on the latest day of Microsoft 365's OneDrive storage trend. The line against each OneDrive's limit comes from the OneDrive usage report.
storageOptimisation.oneDrivePool.nearCap: {count, plural, one {# OneDrive is at 90% or more of its own limit} other {# OneDrives are at 90% or more of their own limits}}. Each OneDrive stops at its own limit, whatever the pool total.
storageOptimisation.oneDrivePool.usedDes: Storage in live OneDrives, as Microsoft's OneDrive usage report lists them. Deleted OneDrives are counted under Deleted but still billing.
storageOptimisation.oneDrivePool.freeDes: What is left of the storage Microsoft allocates to the live OneDrives, each up to its own limit.
storageOptimisation.workload.groupingNot: Grouped by site template, which is what Microsoft Graph reports. These counts will not match the SharePoint admin centre, which groups differently.
storageOptimisation.template.title: Storage by site template
storageOptimisation.template.subtitle: SharePoint storage grouped by the template each site was created from
storageOptimisation.growth.sectionSubtit: Where storage is heading at the current growth rate — and what it costs if nothing changes
storageOptimisation.growth.projectionNot: At {growth} a month, the rate over {window}. Enter the tenant entitlement in Options, Report settings to forecast it against the entitlement.
storageOptimisation.growth.firstDayNote: Microsoft 365 has reported one day of SharePoint storage so far. The forecast starts from the second day it reports.
storageOptimisation.growth.noTrendNote: Microsoft 365's storage trend lists no day with storage for this tenant yet, so this is the total of its site usage report. The forecast starts once the trend has two days.
storageOptimisation.growth.siteReportSou: This is the total of its site usage report: Microsoft 365's storage trend lists no day with storage yet.
This is the total of its site usage report: Microsoft 365's SharePoint storage trend did not come back this time.
storageOptimisation.growth.trendUnreadNo: Microsoft 365's SharePoint storage trend did not come back this time, so this is the total of the site usage report. The forecast returns when Refresh data brings the trend back.
storageOptimisation.growth.window.months: the last {months, plural, one {# month} other {# months}}
storageOptimisation.growth.window.days: the last {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}
storageOptimisation.growth.dailyRateNote: Forecast from {window} of storage: there are fewer than six monthly figures, so treat it as indicative.
storageOptimisation.growth.alreadyExhaus: The tenant is already using more than its pooled entitlement, so there is no future exhaustion date to project. Procurement or cleanup is needed now.
storageOptimisation.growth.estimatedQuot: Your storage quota was estimated from licence counts rather than read from Microsoft, so the headroom and cost figures are approximate.
Your storage quota was estimated from licence counts rather than read from Microsoft, so the headroom is approximate.
storageOptimisation.growth.volatileNote: The monthly figures the rate is derived from are uneven — one month dominates rather than a steady trend — so a single average is a weak guide here. Treat the projection as indicative.
storageOptimisation.growth.impactNote: At the current growth rate the tenant is projected to pass its pooled entitlement on this trajectory. Procurement or cleanup is needed before then.
storageOptimisation.growth.impactNoteNoA: At the current growth rate the tenant is projected to pass its pooled entitlement on this trajectory, but not for years — capacity needs no action today.
storageOptimisation.growth.noExhaustionN: At the current growth rate the tenant stays within its pooled entitlement for at least the next {years} years.
storageOptimisation.growth.cleanUp.title: If inactive and deleted sites are cleaned up
storageOptimisation.growth.cleanUp.count: Counts the {inactive} in live sites with no activity for {years, plural, one {# year} other {# years}} and the {deleted} in deleted sites still billing. Versions are not counted: Microsoft's usage reports do not carry version storage.
storageOptimisation.growth.cleanUp.nothi: Nothing to clean up: no live site has gone {years, plural, one {# year} other {# years}} without activity and no deleted site is still billing, so the line after clean-up is the forecast itself. Versions are not counted: Microsoft's usage reports do not carry version storage.
storageOptimisation.growth.cleanUp.first: {removable} in inactive and deleted sites could be removed today. The forecast after clean-up starts once Microsoft 365 reports a second day of storage.
storageOptimisation.growth.cleanUp.trend: {removable} in inactive and deleted sites could be removed today. The forecast after clean-up returns when Refresh data brings the SharePoint storage trend back.
storageOptimisation.growth.costSubtitle: Extra spend once storage grows past the entitlement, at the configured rate.
storageOptimisation.growth.addedInWindow: Added last {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}

storageOptimisation.offenders.subtitle: The sites and drives driving the most storage
storageOptimisation.offenders.subtitleSi: The sites driving the most storage
storageOptimisation.offenders.subtitleDr: The OneDrives driving the most storage
storageOptimisation.offenders.explain.gr: Storage added between {from} and {to} ({days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}), counted from the first day each site or OneDrive was active in the daily usage reports that came back.
storageOptimisation.offenders.shrinking: Sites & OneDrives that shrank the most
storageOptimisation.offenders.explain.sh: No site or OneDrive measured between {from} and {to} ({days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}) grew. These freed the most storage, counted from the first day each was active in the daily usage reports that came back.
storageOptimisation.offenders.explain.gr: Ranked by storage used on {date}. Measuring growth from Microsoft's daily usage reports did not finish this time; Refresh data tries again.
storageOptimisation.offenders.explain.re: Ranked by storage used on {date}. Growth is measured from Microsoft's daily usage reports, and this report is too old for the panel to read any of them.
storageOptimisation.offenders.explain.no: Ranked by storage used on {date}. Growth is measured from Microsoft's daily usage reports, and none of those from {windowFrom} to {windowTo} came back; Refresh data reads them again after ten minutes.
Ranked by storage used on {date}, because no live site or OneDrive in this report was active in the daily usage reports that came back.
storageOptimisation.offenders.explain.un: Ranked by storage used on {date}, because no site or OneDrive measured between {from} and {to} changed size.
storageOptimisation.offenders.reportsRea: {sitesRead} of the {inWindow} SharePoint and {drivesRead} of the {inWindow} OneDrive daily usage reports from {windowFrom} to {windowTo} came back; Refresh data reads them again after ten minutes.
storageOptimisation.offenders.fastestLoa: Loading the fastest-growing sites and OneDrives
storageOptimisation.offenders.retainedNo: {count} sites and drives are deleted but still consuming quota under retention.
storageOptimisation.offenders.allSubtitl: Every site and drive in the usage reports, sortable and searchable
storageOptimisation.offenders.allSitesSu: Every site in the SharePoint site usage report, sortable and searchable
storageOptimisation.offenders.allDrivesS: Every OneDrive in the OneDrive usage report, sortable and searchable
hiddenName.label: Hidden name
hiddenName.hidden.title: Name hidden in this report
hiddenName.hidden.body: This tab hides site names, owners and links: they are masked before they reach the page, and the report looks up no names. To show them again, open the report with ?hideNames= in the address, unless the site itself is set up to hide names.
hiddenName.concealed.title: Name concealed by Microsoft
hiddenName.concealed.body: Your tenant conceals user and site names in its usage reports, so Microsoft sends hashes instead of names, and the report looks up no names. To show real names: Microsoft 365 admin centre → Settings → Org settings → Reports → uncheck "Display concealed user, group, and site names".
storageOptimisation.hiddenNamesNote: Site names and owners are hidden: they are blurred below, site links are removed, and the report looks up no names. The storage figures are unaffected.
storageOptimisation.concealedNamesNote: Your tenant conceals user and site names in usage reports, so identities below are blurred. The storage figures are unaffected. To show real names: Microsoft 365 admin centre → Settings → Org settings → Reports → uncheck "Display concealed user, group, and site names".
oneDrive.description: How much of the tenant sits in personal OneDrives, who holds the most, and which drives are running out of room.
oneDrive.kpi.usedFromAccountsHint: The total of Microsoft's OneDrive usage report, which lists every OneDrive. Its storage trend lists no day with storage for this tenant yet.
oneDrive.kpi.usedTrendUnreadHint: The total of Microsoft's OneDrive usage report, which lists every OneDrive: its OneDrive storage trend did not come back this time.
oneDrive.kpi.drivesHint: Active drives in the usage report
oneDrive.kpi.nearCapHint: At 90% or more of their own storage quota
oneDrive.kpi.nearCapNone: No drive is close to its quota
oneDrive.kpi.retainedHint: {count} deleted drives still consuming quota under retention
oneDrive.kpi.overLicenceNone: Every drive fits within {entitlement} per user
oneDrive.kpi.overDriveLimitNone: Every drive fits within {limit}, the commonest OneDrive limit
oneDrive.attention.title: Inactive, deleted and unlicensed OneDrives
oneDrive.attention.subtitle: Three separate groups, never added together. A licensed owner's inactive OneDrive adds no storage charge; unlicensed OneDrives, and deleted ones that retention keeps, can be billed once Microsoft archives them.
oneDrive.attention.subtitleNoActivity: Three separate groups, never added together. A licensed owner's inactive OneDrive adds no storage charge; deleted OneDrives that retention keeps can be billed once Microsoft archives them, and so can unlicensed ones, which the quiet group stands in for.
oneDrive.attention.inactiveHint: {count, plural, =0 {No live OneDrive of a licensed owner has gone without activity since {date}.} one {# live OneDrive has had no activity since {date}, or none recorded, and its owner holds a OneDrive licence.} other {# live OneDrives have had no activity since {date}, or none recorded, and their owners hold a OneDrive licence.}} A licensed owner's OneDrive sits inside the licence's storage and adds no storage charge.
oneDrive.attention.inactiveHintNoLicence: {count, plural, =0 {No live OneDrive has gone without activity since {date}.} one {# live OneDrive has had no activity since {date}, or none recorded.} other {# live OneDrives have had no activity since {date}, or none recorded.}} Microsoft's active-user report did not come back or matched none of the owners, so some of these may belong to owners without a licence, which can be billed.
oneDrive.attention.deletedHint: {count, plural, =0 {No deleted OneDrive is held.} one {# deleted OneDrive is held until its retention period ends. Its owner has no licence, so if retention keeps it past 93 days it is archived and, once billing for unlicensed OneDrives is on, billed like one.} other {# deleted OneDrives are held until their retention period ends. Their owners have no licence, so any that retention keeps past 93 days are archived and, once billing for unlicensed OneDrives is on, billed like one.}} Deleted OneDrives are not part of the SharePoint entitlement.
oneDrive.attention.unlicensedHint: {count, plural, =0 {No live OneDrive belongs to an owner without a OneDrive licence.} one {# live OneDrive belongs to an owner without a OneDrive licence.} other {# live OneDrives belong to owners without a OneDrive licence.}} {notListed, plural, =0 {} one {# of them is counted because Microsoft's licence report, which lists licensed users, does not list its owner: that owner most likely holds no licence.} other {# of them are counted because Microsoft's licence report, which lists licensed users, does not list their owners: those owners most likely hold no licence.}} Microsoft makes an unlicensed OneDrive read-only after 60 days and archives it after 93; once billing for unlicensed OneDrives is on, archived storage costs $0.05 per GB a month (not for EDU, GCC or DoD tenants).
oneDrive.attention.noActivityHint: {count, plural, =0 {No live OneDrive active within the last {years, plural, one {# year} other {# years}} has gone without activity since {since}.} one {# live OneDrive has had no activity since {since}, though it was active within the last {years, plural, one {# year} other {# years}} (longer quiet ones count as inactive).} other {# live OneDrives have had no activity since {since}, though they were active within the last {years, plural, one {# year} other {# years}} (longer quiet ones count as inactive).}} Shown in place of the owners without a licence, because Microsoft's active-user report, which lists the licensed owners, did not come back or matched none of them: an unlicensed owner's OneDrive goes quiet, and Microsoft archives it {days} days after the licence goes. Once billing for unlicensed OneDrives is on, archived storage costs $0.05 per GB a month (not for EDU, GCC or DoD tenants).
oneDrive.attention.bandsTitle: How long the inactive OneDrives have been inactive
oneDrive.attention.bandsSubtitle: {count, plural, one {# inactive OneDrive} other {# inactive OneDrives}}, by time since the last activity
oneDrive.attention.bandsEmpty: No live OneDrive has gone {years, plural, one {# year} other {# years}} without activity.
oneDrive.overLicence.title: OneDrives over their licensed storage
oneDrive.overLicence.subtitle: Accounts holding more OneDrive storage than any licence in the tenant includes ({entitlement} per user)
oneDrive.overLicence.subtitleSet: Accounts holding more than the {entitlement} of OneDrive storage per user set in Report settings
oneDrive.overLicence.titleDriveLimit: OneDrives over the usual OneDrive limit
oneDrive.overLicence.subtitleDriveLimit: Accounts holding more than {limit}, the commonest storage limit: {reporting} of {count, plural, one {# live OneDrive} other {# live OneDrives}} {reporting, plural, one {reports} other {report}} it
oneDrive.overLicence.label: OneDrives over licensed storage
oneDrive.overLicence.note: Measured against the most generous plan the tenant holds: 5 TB on E3, E5, G3 and G5 with five or more licences, 1 TB on Business plans, 2 GB on frontline. Microsoft does not report which licence each user holds; set a different figure in Options, Report settings.
oneDrive.overLicence.noteSet: Measured against the figure set in Options, Report settings. Clear it there to go back to the estimate from licences.
oneDrive.overLicence.noteDriveLimit: The report has no access to the tenant's licences (the Organization.Read.All permission was not granted), so this measures against the commonest storage limit among the OneDrives, usually the tenant's default: a OneDrive listed here most likely has had its limit raised. Set the licensed figure in Options, Report settings.
oneDrive.overLicence.noteDriveLimitNoSiz: None of the tenant's licences has a OneDrive allowance this report knows (education allowances vary by agreement; developer and add-on plans are not sized here), so this measures against the commonest storage limit among the OneDrives, usually the tenant's default: a OneDrive listed here most likely has had its limit raised. Set the licensed figure in Options, Report settings.
oneDrive.overLicence.noteSetNoEstimate: Measured against the figure set in Options, Report settings. The tenant's licences give no estimate, so clearing it measures against the commonest OneDrive limit.
